tob-10221: In these famous 1902 lectures, the philosopher William James studies religious experience the way psychologists study anything else — by collecting firsthand accounts of conversion, prayer, and mystical moments. He treats saints and mystics as case studies, asking what their experiences reveal about human nature rather than whether their beliefs are true. The book founded the psychology of religion and remains one of the most readable works of American philosophy.
tob-10521: Published in 1908, The Kybalion claims to reveal the secret Hermetic teachings of ancient Egypt and Greece in seven principles — mentalism, correspondence, vibration, and the rest. Written by the mysterious ‘Three Initiates,’ it became a bible of New Thought and modern occultism. Whether ancient wisdom or clever invention, it has influenced spiritual seekers for over a century.
tob-4021: The second volume of Locke’s Essay takes up words and knowing — how speech works, how we know what we claim to know, and where reason has to stop. Books 3 and 4 finish his case that all our grasp of things grows from experience. Few works of thought have changed the world more quietly than this one.
tob-0121: Ex-congressman Ignatius Donnelly’s 1882 book held that a great island realm — Atlantis — sank under the Atlantic, seeding the high cultures of Egypt and the Americas. tob-0021: The Acts of Paul and Thecla trails a young noblewoman who quits her bridegroom to follow the apostle Paul, preaching and baptizing through Asia Minor.
